Those kinds of stories -- whether that particular case is accurate or not, these were the kinds of things happening. It wasn't -- the point of so-called ethnic cleansing is the point of human contact, largely. I mean, some people will flee because they know what's coming, and that's part of the campaign, is to make people without actually forcibly removing them if you can. But for the forcible removal, whether it's killing or expulsion, you do it, yeah, as we would be in this room with somebody pointing something at one of the others and saying, This is what you have to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So therefore, the absence of heavy artillery didn't necessarily mean that it would be impossible to implement some form of ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: No, it doesn't mean it's impossible to implement a form of ethnic cleansing because it takes place at that level, where that -- where it's possible to carry out that kind of action.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the small weaponry that could possibly assist, if not provoke ethnic cleansing, would that be weapons like pistols, rifles, or rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: It can be any kind of -- any piece of weaponry. It some cases in northwestern Bosnia, armoured vehicles and tanks were blowing away houses. In other cases, it could be something like a pitchfork, I guess; a knife, any sort of small arms that was man-portable, that you could point at somebody and say, If you don't do this, this weapon will be used against you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: This map is already marked 367. I would ask that it be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have reservations about this map for the reason which has been discussed, because it shows the enclaves as a contiguous territory. Notwithstanding the clarification that has been offered by Dr. Gow, it appears to us that there may be confusion down the line because Srebrenica was cut off, as this witness has said, and the map should reflect that. Perhaps if the Prosecution could produce a new version which shows that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, it's going to be admitted as it is, with the understanding that it's not a faithful reproduction of the reality of the situation on the ground. I suppose, Ms. Sellers, you take the hint of --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. And we appreciate learned counsel, and that's why we certainly did want to inform the Trial Chamber that there had been a slight misrepresentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime this is being admitted as Prosecution Exhibit P367. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, was there any action or reaction on behalf of Bosnian Serbs that accompanied the military -- Serbian military preparation that you earlier testified about?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: There was a political dimension to the state project that involved preparations through the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party, to prepare the way for takeover. In December, instructions were issued to begin preparations, preparations which would involve the creation at a designated point of crisis headquarters, with two operational plans, depending on the particular circumstances, whether or not there was already an ethnic Serbian majority in the area or whether the Serbs were not in a majority. Those plans would involve identification of non-Serbs who were potentially politically significant to be immediately detained. It included plans for creating a new Serbian government in the particular municipality. It included instructions for coordinating with the security centres within the Serbian-controlled territories, that is, interior ministry, police, security service forces, and also for coordinating with the JNA wherever possible, and for coordinating with the plans. So it would be, in a sense, a political part of the strategy of takeover in which the SDS-organised ethnic Serb party would take control and would be relating politically and militarily to all elements within the situation. In line with that, already from April 1991, i.e., a year before the independence of Bosnia and Herzegovina and a year before the onset of major armed hostilities, a process had begun of creating associations of Serbian municipalities. By September 1991, this had become the declaration of so-called Serbian Autonomous Regions designated sometimes, when you read them, as SAOs. Those areas, and two had already been created in Croatia as part of the phase of the war there, and in September 1991, between the 12th and the 19th, four of them were created in Bosnia and Herzegovina; a fifth one was later to be created in November. These were part of creating the political infrastructure to go with the preparations for use of armed force to secure the takeover and control of these territories as part of the project to create this Serbian state, statelet, unit within, whatever it was going to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you to look at the next document. It also has been premarked 281, and the English version bears the ERN number 03014245. Dr. Gow, could you look at that document and tell the Trial Chamber its relationship to these autonomous regions that you have just testified about.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: This is a newspaper report from the newspaper "Javnost," which reports described the creation of the first of those Serbian Autonomous Regions, the Serbian Autonomous Region of Herzegovina, which was declared on the 12th of September. Subsequently, the Bosnian Krajina, I think it was on the 14th, Semberija, or North-Eastern Bosnia, on the 17th, and Sarajevo Romanija on the 19th. I might have got the order of those -- I'm not entirely sure of the order off the top of my head. And then one for Northern Bosnia was declared later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, were these autonomous regions still part of Bosnia, the Republic of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: They are part of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a sovereign state that was, at that stage, still operating formally within the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia -- and this is the point in 1991 -- and of the sovereign state of Bosnia-Herzegovina which acted outside of that Socialist Federative Republic context once the dissolution process had been completed. The association of municipalities is something, as I understand it, that was permitted, also in terms of the law. The declaration of autonomous regions and so forth was kind of extralegal activity in the political domain, moving towards what would ultimately be the declaration of a state, the state of the Serbian people, the Republic of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the registrar, could we please use the number that's been designated and mark this as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P281.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is being so admitted and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P281. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, did there come a time period when the Bosnian Serbs within the territory of Bosnia took other political steps in order to increase their political autonomy within that territory?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Yes, they did. Again, we made some reference to some of this earlier. After this period of declaration of autonomous regions in September, there was a plebiscite in the so-called Serbian-controlled areas in October or November, which, again, I should know this clearly but I don't remember exactly off the top of my head, which was to decide to assert the will of the Serbian people of these areas to remain part of Federal Yugoslavia, the context also the Bosnian part, movement asserting the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina. By the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, steps were taken to declare the Serbian -- the Republic of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina, so a further step along that way, including that a Serbian assembly had been created within that context, all parts of steps moving towards the projected statehood element of the project and to separating territories from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might I now turn your attention to the next document in the binder. It has already received the number P288. That's in the B/C/S version, and the English number is 288E. Dr. Gow, would you please look at the English version. I would like to draw your attention to the title, but also to what appears to be Article 1 of this document. Would you explain to the Trial Chamber the importance of Article 1 within framing the growing political independence of Bosnian Serbs on the territory.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Yes. But if I may, first of all, for the record, also point out what might be another deficiency, I would say, about the translation. This should actually read, on the proclamation of the Republic of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is what it says in the original, not the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that's a distinction at least of a small kind for an academic, if not anybody else, which matters, because later on there will be a change of name. Article 1 makes reference to the Serbian autonomous areas, I think showing the heritage as part of this -- of the stages in this plan to build this Serbian statelet. And it alludes to regions in which the Serbian people remained in a minority because of the genocide conducted against it in the Second World War. So this is laying claim to territories -- the plebiscite 9th and 10th of December, sorry, not November. I wasn't sure of the date, but we have it. So this is laying claim to territories where all ethnic Serbs are at that moment the majority and dominant population, but also to some territories where it is said, as a result of the Second World War, they are no longer a majority but it's presumed would have been had things -- had events of the Second World War not taken place. So this is laying claim to territory, and a further element in building the political structure within this part of the project.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now would you draw your attention to Article 2 and to see how that explains the relationship between this declaration, the Bosnian Serb people, to the former Yugoslav Republic, or what would now be moving toward dissolution. Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber that relationship.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Article 2 designates that this putative republic of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina was recognising Bosnia-Herzegovina in the title, is asserting that it's part of federal -- of the federal Yugoslav state. It's notable that it already is cautious in use of the term "Federal Yugoslav state" because it's coming at a moment where the SFRY is still in a process of dissolution. So it's kind of phrased to go whichever way other events might turn. But the clear thing is that it's identifying the association with the federal Yugoslav state, which implicitly means with Serbia in this context.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, I would ask you to turn the page so that the Trial Chamber can be informed of the date of this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: The declaration was the 9th of January, 1992, which again, for clarity on the record, in this process, was between the invitation on the 16th, 17th of December from the European Council to invite applications for recognition of independent international personality but before the advisory commission had reported back and before the European Council had made decisions on the way forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the person who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Momcilo Krajisnik has signed it as the president of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the registry, could we maintain the P number, and I would ask the Trial Chamber, could we submit this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The number will be P288.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document is being admitted as Prosecution Exhibit P288. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, in furtherance to the reaction of Bosnian Serbs to the dissolution of the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, did there come a time when the Assembly of Serbian People proclaimed their independence?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: This declaration, and also later a proclamation of a constitution, were put in place and were subject to a declaration of independence on or around the 7th of April, 1992, at which point there was broad international recognition of the independent international personality of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and so this was taken as part of the plan. Now Bosnia-Herzegovina's change of status had been confirmed, this part of the Serbian initiative went into action, and so to declare it separate from the otherwise independent state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, breaching, of course, the territorial integrity and the sovereign rights of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as would otherwise be understood.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask you now to turn to the next document in your binder. It has ERN number 01367471 in the English version. The B/C/S version follows. Dr. Gow, I would really like to ask you what you have just testified about concerning the independence of Bosnia, the proclamation of independence of the Bosnian Serb people. Is that reflected in the document that you're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: It is. This is a report from the 7th of April, 1992, noting that the Serbian assembly -- the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina had met that morning and had declared independence. It also notes at the same time that the two members, Serbian members, to the collective leadership in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mrs. Plavsic and Dr. Koljevic, had resigned, thereby indicating withdrawal from collective political processes in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did the Bosnian Serb people therefore start to take on a separate political identity within the territory of Bosnia at this point?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: I think if we were to approach that accurately, what we would say is that they already had clearly been laying claim to a separate political identity. That's what this story of steps from the association of municipalities through to the declaration of a republic of Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so on, and through to this point. What this is doing is actually say, in a way, no longer that it's part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was maintained as part of the political ambiguity while Bosnia-Herzegovina was not yet recognised as having an independent international personality, but now they're saying it is no longer part of Bosnia-Herzegovina. At this point they're withdrawing from Bosnia-Herzegovina as the state, and they are saying this is going to be a separate -- this is declared as a separate entity.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Might I ask for a P number from the registrar for this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. It will be P413.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We should also point out, just again to add to these things, that the statement also notes that it would -- that this can or will be joined in union with Serbia or with other entities in this Yugoslav federation. That goes back to something I said earlier about the terminology. Whether you call Great Serbia or Kadijevic's new Yugoslavia or some other association of Serbian states, this here is being phrased in that context, and I think "other entities" would also imply the Republic of Serbian Krajina as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, this document is being admitted in evidence and marked Prosecution Exhibit 413.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, in continuance with our examination of the growing political separation between ethnic groups within Bosnia, did there come a time period when the Bosnian Serb people decided to have their own constitution?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Okay. The Serbian entity -- the Republic of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina promulgated a constitution on the 28th of February, 1992, putting in place the preparations, again, for the separation and the declaration of a separate unit from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you to turn to the next document in your binder. In the original B/C/S, it's ERN number 00359816. Dr. Gow, I'd ask you to turn to the English version of that document. The ERN number is 00359826. Dr. Gow, I'd like to draw your attention to the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Which is proclaiming the constitution of the republic -- for the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. And then I would like you to also look at Articles 1, 2, 3, and 4, and if you would be so kind as to describe them and give the Trial Chamber your expert opinion on what they mean in terms of the political nature now of the Serbian people. I believe it's on the screen also.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: It is. Article 1 indicates that we now have this Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in the sense that it's a state of the Serbian people and of all citizens living therein. I know where this is going, so I would draw your attention to the "all citizens living therein," because later on that element will be removed. Article 2, again, makes reference to the Serbian Autonomous Regions, to the territorial composition of this construct, and again, reference to the territories on which genocide was committed against Serb people in the Second World War. And Article 3, again, reiterates that it's linked to the federal state of Yugoslavia. So, again, making clear that whatever the reference to Bosnia-Herzegovina, it is clearly part of this federal Yugoslav project, state, entity, whichever one it's going to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. And is that also the reason that Article 6 states that the citizens of the republic have citizenship in the republic and of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Yes, that would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would also ask that this be given a number by the registrar, and I would like to submit this constitution into evidence for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P414.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document, Ms. Sellers, is being admitted in evidence and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P414. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, moving along, I'd like to turn your attention to the next document in the binder, an Official Gazette. In B/C/S the number is 00897223. In English, the ERN is 0048063. Dr. Gow, might I draw your attention, in the English version, to the date of this document, and please explain to the Trial Chamber what the document is.

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: We saw before the 28th of February constitution of the Republic of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina, this is the constitution -- revised constitution of this entity from the 17th of December, 1992. You will note the name has been changed from the Republic of the Serbian People of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the constitution of the Republika Srpska, first of all. If you move down to Article 1, you'll note that the Republika Srpska is the state of the Serb people. In the February constitution, I pointed out the reference to "and all citizens therein." That has been removed. If you move further, you look at the continuing consistency of a kind within Article 2 the territory consists of the regions of the Serb ethnic entities, still noting the regions of genocide, and giving the authority to change borders and status only to the Serb people through a plebiscite. And in Article 3, you get the continuing reference to being part of the federal state of Yugoslavia. So by now there's been a complete declaration of independence, there's a new constitution which clearly and unambiguously identifies the ethnic Serb character of this policy, that continues to assert a link to a federal Yugoslavia, which is in clear contrast to the declaration of independence from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask the registrar also, could we have a number for the document for the Prosecution, and then I would ask the Trial Chamber to tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be P415.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document, Ms. Sellers, is being admitted into evidence and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P415.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, throughout this time period, meaning from the spring of 1992, throughout 1992 until the end, was the hostility, the armed conflict or the fighting relating to the declaration of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina continuing?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: Yes. The armed conflict continued from the starting point in March/April 1992 through until November 199 -- possibly in some kind of small ways beyond, but to the end of November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did the Bosnian government continue to structure, consolidate, and form armed forces that it was using to defend its territorial integrity during 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: It did. We discussed earlier the initial turning to the Territorial Defence system, the declaration of forming an army, the later new declaration of forming an army. It was an evolving situation in which the Bosnian authorities were trying to create an armed force to -- that would serve their purposes and interests as they sought to combat the Serbian and, at times, Croatian campaigns to compromise Bosnia's territorial integrity. That was an evolution which was affected by the relative absence of certain categories of weapons a lot of the time; it was affected by political factors at times; and it's one which I think that, even by that point, at the end of 1995, was probably not complete.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I please ask you to look at the next document in the binder, and it's already been premarked P279. The English version has been marked P279E. Dr. Gow, could you please tell the Trial Chamber, is this document related to your testimony that you've just given concerning the continuing formation of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: It is. It relates to a decision in August 1992 formally, having declared an army previously, formally to declare the organisational structure for that army, indicating that there would be five corps operating in the five different regions with Bosnia-Herzegovina, with their command in the places indicated on the map here -- indicated in the list here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. And the list that you're referring to, is that the list of places that one finds on the subsequent page of the document as shown on the sanctions, or are you referring to the list of the different corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: I'm looking at the list of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th Corps, which is identified underneath the decision on that forming of corps of the army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the zones of responsibility and subordination. This is about attempting to give formal structure to the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina and consolidating some of the arrangements which have been emerging in this period.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: If you'd please turn to the next page of that document, and midway through the first half of the document, it refers to now the different geographical locations of the corps of the army. Would you please indicate for the Trial Chamber whether Srebrenica is located in the 2nd Corps, not according to the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDREW JAMES WILLIAM GOW
utterances.text: The document indicates that within the 2nd Corps area of responsibility Srebrenica is one of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would ask that we use the P number assigned. I would ask that this also be able to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can confirm it will be P279.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. So this document is being admitted and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P279. Thank you. Whenever it's convenient for you, Ms. Sellers, we have got another two minutes. It's up to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to say that I could complete in two minutes, but to be very honest, I think I do need another 15 minutes, and so I think it might be more beneficial to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Since I'm not feeling well at all, we'll send me home a little bit earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can send me home a little earlier too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am deteriorating from minute to minute, actually. I'm really feeling unwell. The sitting is adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Are we sitting in the same courtroom or in another courtroom tomorrow? Same courtroom. Okay. Thank you, Dr. Gow. May I just remind you that you're not to communicate with anyone. You know what the rule is. I thank you. We'll reconvene at tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you. 18

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, 23 November 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
